newsitem.title: MACEDONIA: Macedonia inflation quickens to 0.3 pct in Sept.
newsitem.headline: Macedonia inflation quickens to 0.3 pct in Sept.

text.p: Macedonia's monthly consumer price inflation quickened to 0.3 percent in September from deflation of -0.7 percent in August, the National Bank of Macedonia said.
Inflation traditionally falls in summer months due to low prices on farm goods and picks up in September, said an NBM official who declined to named.
Annual inflation in this former Yugoslav republic this year is seen between 2.5 and three percent.

Macedonia's inflation has dropped sharply from 2,000 percent in 1993 and 55 percent in 1994 to nine percent last year, as a result of a stringent reform programme backed by international lending institutions.
